faqs.a: It walks your JSON and emits one TypeScript interface per object: each key becomes a typed property, nested objects become their own interfaces, and arrays become typed arrays.
faqs.q: How does JSON to TypeScript work?

faqs.a: JSON strings become string, numbers become number, booleans become boolean, null stays null, arrays become T[] with the item type inferred, and objects become named interfaces.
faqs.q: How are JSON types mapped to TypeScript types?

faqs.a: It collects the distinct inferred item types and builds a union: [1, "a"] becomes (number | string)[]. Empty arrays fall back to unknown[].
Enable the optional-properties toggle: every property gets a ? suffix (name?: string). Useful for partial API responses where fields may be absent.
faqs.q: Can I make all properties optional?

faqs.a: Yes - the export toggle adds or removes the export keyword on every interface, so the output drops into modules or ambient declaration files as needed.
faqs.q: Does it add the export keyword?

faqs.a: It is a starting point: add readonly, JSDoc comments, or stricter literal types to taste. Always review generated code before shipping.

json-typescript.formula:
value -> TypeScript type:
  "text"          -> string
  42 / 3.14        -> number
  true / false     -> boolean
  null             -> null
  [T, T]           -> T[]
  [1, "a"]         -> (number | string)[]
  []               -> unknown[]
  { ... }          -> interface named after the key (PascalCase)
options: export keyword on/off, optional (?) on/off

keyFacts: JSON to TypeScript converts any JSON document into TypeScript interfaces.
Every object becomes an interface; every key becomes a typed property.
Strings map to string, numbers to number, booleans to boolean, null stays null.
Arrays become T[] with inferred item types; mixed arrays become union arrays like (number | string)[].
Original key names are preserved; invalid identifiers are safely quoted.
Optional export keywords and optional (?) properties adapt the output to your codebase.
json-typescript.keywords: json to typescript, json to ts interface, convert json to typescript, json typescript generator, json to interface online
limitations: Type inference reads one sample: fields that vary in type across responses need manual unions.
Null stays null rather than a union with undefined - adjust to your strictness settings.
No JSDoc, readonly modifiers, or literal types are generated - add them yourself.
Very deep documents produce many interfaces; consider splitting them manually.
